result: I found that the PF₆⁻ counter-anion is disordered and submitted a two-site model of it; the rest of the structure (the Ru complex) is ordered and I left it unchanged. In the original model the anion's displacement parameters were very large: Ueq was up to 0.30 Å² on the fluorines and 0.11 Å² on P3. The largest difference-map peaks (up to 1.06 e/Å³) all sat around it, about 1.5 Å from P3. Four of those peaks lay between the equatorial F atoms, consistent with the anion rotating about the F2–P3–F4 axis. I kept P3, F2 and F4 shared and split the four equatorial fluorines into PART 1 (F1/F3/F5/F6) and PART 2 (F7–F10), with occupancies tied to free variable 2. It refined to 0.554 / 0.446. Restraints are SADI on the P–F and cis F···F distances, SIMU and RIGU on the anion, and ISOR on P3, F2 and F4. The first refinement attempt failed numerically; it ran once I refined the new fluorines isotropically first and then made them anisotropic. The fit improved from R1 0.0436 / wR2 0.1074 / GooF 1.28 to R1 0.0418 / wR2 0.1018 / GooF 1.22, and the largest difference peak fell to 0.78 e/Å³. Peaks of about 0.5–0.7 e/Å³ remain close to the anion fluorines, and their displacement parameters are still large. That suggests the anion is also smeared out somewhat beyond the two modelled positions.
